scope.speaker: agent
scope.text: Canon (owner-ratified sheet, wording superseded by R14): the Deep Desert Tribes work the fire; the flame harvest is controlled burns on their schedule with the burn-line walked for scorch-fruit; an unplanned burn is answered by arson-justice, short furious raids. The sheet's 'fire-farmers' is struck by R14.

scope.speaker: agent
scope.text: Ruling recorded in About.xml: 'they are FIRE HARVESTERS, and they are the Deep Tribes ... the Pyre burns with or without them' -> the rite is a fraction of the fire clock, never all of it.

scope.speaker: agent
scope.text: Owner note 2026-09-26 (no tsn on that event, so not citable as OWNER:): the Deep Tribes do light fires in the Pyrelands, just not with flamethrowers or industrial firebombs. The rite's torch-lighting fits this.

scope.speaker: agent
scope.text: PYRELANDS_RM_MOD_BUILD_1 §6 moved the franchise-free burn-line, arson tally, fire-hawk and furnace-beast to mandrake.rm.pyrelands; this mod keeps only what names the Deep Desert Tribes (a campaign faction).

Freeze ruling R14: no fire-farmers as a distinct people; the owner: 'They are not "farmers," I have never liked that term.' They are FIRE HARVESTERS, the Deep Tribes, coming periodically for their sacred fire rites and to reap the bounty, then returning to the deep desert; the Pyre burns with or without them.

asks.speaker: agent
asks.text: Picture the one moment that makes you say 'that is the Pyrelands Tribes'. Is it a small file of Tribes walking in with a covered coal, lighting the grass themselves, then working the black behind the front for scorch-fruit? Or a short furious raid arriving the morning after your colony set a fire it should not have? (This picks the first showcase.)

review.by: rm-judge a4076b10482d95ea4 (fresh Opus, not the author)
review.why: Asks the same rite-or-raid question the root's judged-first line already answers; he can correct that line through ask_root.

asks.speaker: agent
asks.text: The flame-harvest visit today walks a party to the centre of a burn already standing and then they leave; they pick nothing (the code says the sheet only asked for them to be SEEN farming the fire). The rite party, by contrast, really picks scorch-fruit and carries it off. When you watch the visit party reach the fire, what do you expect to see them doing there?

asks.speaker: agent
asks.text: Arson debt builds silently from every fire your colony owns, your tamed fire-hawk and furnace-beast included, until a raid lands. Before that raid, should you have been able to see the debt growing (a goodwill warning, a letter, a number somewhere), or is the surprise the point?
Is the paragraph above the Deep Tribes in the Pyrelands? Correct any word, or say "yes". (the paragraph: turn_01.md)
asks.decision: The root text: what the Deep Tribes do in the Pyrelands and what the mod is judged on first; stage 1 cannot end without his approval of it.
asks.author: rm-role-designer-1793866044

review.by: rm-judge a4076b10482d95ea4 (fresh Opus, not the author)
review.why: Settles the root, answerable in a phrase, offers no removal. Fixed on review: the line catches at the lead harvester (no lighting job); a raid comes only if the goodwill hit makes them hostile, debt decays; raid 0.6x with a 250-point floor so 'usually smaller'; after the raid only the debt clears and the Tribes stay at war (no rites while hostile); a shot-at party defends itself; any colony-attributed fire counts; the check is Pyrelands biome, not home map; R14 harvester wording attributed to the ruling, not quoted as his.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: The thornvine nutrition patch serves the furnace-beast's thermal cycle, which moved to franchise-free mandrake.rm.pyrelands, but the patch stayed in this campaign mod. On a load without this mod JobDriver_Ingest refuses thornvine (no nutrition), so the beast's 'one of the only things that strips a thornvine patch' line silently breaks. A Relentless fix (move the patch), not a question for him.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Both fix items show 'implemented' 2026-10-15 and were reassigned twice since, but never closed; their fixes are in the code. Each needs its live proof (the route-through-fire row stays UNMEASURED), which this pass's scenes should supply.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Two built mechanisms put Tribes at a burn: the flame-harvest visit (walks to the fire, leaves, picks nothing) and the rite (lights it, picks scorch-fruit, carries it off). The sheet's 'burn-line walked for scorch-fruit' is only met by the rite. What the visit should look like at the fire is for him (ask a_harvest_visit_at_the_fire); neither is put up for removal.

lacks: asserted start (Pyrelands map, burn standing, Tribes present/non-hostile)
entry point: needs a proof hook to read/set the arson debt
control: lightning-only burn accrues no debt
entry point lighting N-1 / N fires

script_audit.scene: fire rite end to end (none staged in this mod's script; RM Pyrelands has rite_harvest_route_avoids_fire UNMEASURED)
lacks: any entry point that forces TrySend
start assertion (pods behind a lit line)
control (rite disabled -> plain front, no party)

failure_modes: He never sees it: every mechanism needs a Pyrelands home map, a live burn-line and fire clock, a present non-hostile Tribes faction, and then a roll (rite fraction, storyteller chance, min fires); nothing has ever been run live end to end, so in real play it may simply never fire and nothing says why.

It reads wrong when it fires: the visit party walks to the fire and leaves without harvesting (a pointless visitor, not a farmer), harvesters path through the flames or burn, or a rite party ends in a fight; the Tribes then look like victims or tourists instead of the fire's farmers.

The punishment feels arbitrary: arson debt grows invisibly from any colony-owned fire, his tamed fire-hawk and furnace-beast included, and a raid lands with no warning he could act on; or the franchise split breaks quietly (thornvine left in the wrong tier) so a neighbour's mechanic fails on a load without this mod.
